summary: A podcast-style customer interview focusing on NovaInsights' experience deploying Redwood for production LLM inference. Discussion covers performance improvements, cost savings, security posture, and marketing outcomes. The tone is conversational; intent is a 20-30 minute edited podcast plus social clips and a written case study.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Welcome everyone, thanks for joining the NovaInsights x Redwood chat, I'm Jordan from Redwood, we've got Priya, Alex, and our guests Marta, Daniel, and Lina. This is being recorded for a short customer story podcast.
[00:20] Marta: Thanks, really excited.
[00:25] Alex: Quick note, we'll edit for time and pull a few highlight clips, any concerns?
[00:32] Marta: No, that's fine, go ahead.
[00:35] Jordan: Great. So to start, can you give us a quick one-two minute overview of NovaInsights and the problem you were trying to solve?
[00:45] Marta: Sure, NovaInsights is a market intelligence startup, we help product teams surface trends from customer conversations. Um we had increasing latency and cost issues when we scaled our summarization and semantic search workflows, and, um, we also needed stronger controls for enterprise customers on data residency.
[01:10] Daniel: Yeah, the context: we ingest call transcripts and user feedback, run embeddings and multi-turn summarization. Our prior stack used a managed LLM endpoint plus lots of shimming which, uh, made costs unpredictable and latency jittery during spikes.
[01:30] Priya: When you say jittery, what numbers were you seeing?
[01:33] Daniel: Typical p95 around 1.2s for single-turn, but for long contexts p95 could go past 3s which impacted our realtime UI. During batch jobs cost spiked, monthly inference bills doubled in quarters with heavy data reprocessing.
[01:48] Jordan: Got it, and what led you to try Redwood specifically?
[01:52] Marta: We liked the developer experience — the API was easy to integrate — but really the pitch was predictable economics and the dedicated option for enterprise customers. Also security controls like KMS and private VPC mattered for some of our clients in health and finance.
[02:10] Lina: Another thing: Redwood's team helped us run a mini-benchmark, and that showed a couple of model variants that hit our latency targets while cutting per-token cost. That sealed it.
[02:27] Alex: Nice — can you share specific impact after rolling into prod?
[02:31] Daniel: After switching critical routes to Redwood Dedicated, p95 latency for the UI flows dropped from ~2s to ~650ms. Token costs dropped by about 35% thanks to batching and the quantized model profile we adopted. Overall customer-facing incidents related to inference fell from three per quarter to zero in the last two quarters.
[02:55] Marta: From a marketing frame, our demo conversion improved because the product feels snappier. We used a clip of the UX in our webinar and got better engagement.
[03:05] Jordan: That's great, curious on the deployment: you used Dedicated for prod and Hosted for light workloads?
[03:11] Daniel: Exactly. Dev and early prod used Redwood Hosted while heavy traffic routes and regulated customer tenants were pinned to Dedicated in our AWS VPC. The private deployment options and KMS made procurement happy.
[03:25] Priya: Any challenges during onboarding?
[03:28] Daniel: A bit of model tuning and cache warm-up — the KV cache and batching defaults needed adjustment for our long histories. Priya and the SE team helped with tuning policies which improved hit rates and latency. The docs were decent but some infra docs used different names for concepts, small mismatch.
[03:50] Priya: Thanks, we'll flag that.
[03:52] Jordan: For listeners who care about security: can you talk briefly about compliance needs and what mattered most?
[03:58] Marta: SOC 2 was baseline, then we needed tenant isolation, audit logs, and customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM). Redwood's audit logs and SSO/SAML integration made it straightforward to satisfy our security team and clients.
[04:15] Lina: Also data residency — some clients wanted EU-only processing; the routing policies and regional endpoints were helpful.
[04:23] Alex: We'll include a link to the security brief in the episode notes.
[04:27] Jordan: Marketing angle — how did NovaInsights use the story?
[04:31] Marta: We spun up a webinar, published a case study, and did a short customer testimonial on the site. The podcast here will be another asset. We track MQLs from these pieces; the Redwood case study was in our top three performers for quarter.
[04:47] Daniel: One anecdote — a large prospect asked about latency during a sales call, we were able to demo a live query hitting the dedicated endpoints, helped close a deal.
[04:58] Jordan: Were there any vendor comparisons during evaluation?
[05:01] Marta: We tested a couple of other providers for ease-of-use, but cost modeling and the ability to pin model versions were differentiators. Also, Redwood's quality monitoring and rollout controls eased our concern about regression risk when switching models.
[05:19] Priya: On quality regressions — did you run evals and regression alerts?
[05:22] Lina: Yes, we set up a small eval harness and Redwood's alerts triggered once during a model rollout, which saved us from shipping a change that would have worsened summary quality.
[05:34] Jordan: Fantastic. For the podcast, listeners love concrete numbers — can you repeat the headline metrics?
[05:38] Daniel: Sure — latency p95 from ~2s to ~650ms on critical UI routes; token cost reduction roughly 35% on heavy workloads; incidents related to inference down from three per quarter to zero.
[05:51] Marta: Engagement improvement on our demo pages by ~18% after improvements, which we correlate to the faster experience.
[05:58] Jordan: Great soundbites. Now, anything unexpected after adoption?
[06:02] Marta: We were surprised by how much the model compaction options reduced compute without losing quality. Also the rollout tools let our product team iterate faster, fewer rollback headaches.
[06:15] Alex: Any tips for teams getting started?
[06:18] Daniel: Start with a small benchmark, identify the critical routes, test dedicated for the hot paths. Also invest in prefix caching and batch tuning early.
[06:28] Lina: And involve security early — provisioning KMS and SSO took longer than we expected but saved time later.
[06:36] Jordan: Perfect. For marketing quotes, do you have 2-3 lines you’d be happy to have on an external case study?
[06:43] Marta: Yeah — "Redwood helped NovaInsights cut inference costs while making our product noticeably faster for customers." And "The dedicated deployment and security integrations let us sell into regulated accounts we couldn't before."
[06:57] Alex: We'll fine-tune wording with Marta and send for approval.
[07:02] Jordan: Quick technical aside for listeners — can you summarize how you route requests between hosted and dedicated?
[07:07] Daniel: We use request tagging in our gateway. Low-risk non-customer-facing batch jobs go to Hosted, interactive UI requests are routed to Dedicated pool in region. In failover we fall back to a compatible hosted model for non-sensitive tenancy.
[07:26] Priya: Did you run into any scale events?
[07:29] Daniel: We had a holiday traffic spike, Redwood's autoscaling burst handled it; we used a temporary higher-priority queue to avoid tail latency increases.
[07:39] Marta: It was seamless for customers.
[07:42] Jordan: For procurement listeners, what was the buying process like?
[07:46] Marta: We did an RFP for inference providers, Redwood's dedicated commitment pricing and the security package made it easy. Procurement liked the clear SLAs. Docs and the support from Redwood's CS team closed gaps quickly.
[08:00] Alex: Any hesitations from legal or procurement?
[08:03] Marta: Legal wanted the data processing addendum and some residency clauses, nothing blocking. Redwood's privacy and DPA template helped.
[08:12] Jordan: Great. Open mic — any stories or favorite wins using the system?
[08:16] Lina: We instrumented a cohort analysis where we saw upsell rates grow for power users after we improved response times.
[08:23] Daniel: Also, the daily cost dashboard in the Redwood Console helped us spot a misconfigured route that was burning tokens early on. Caught it within a day.
[08:35] Jordan: Love that. As we come to a close, final ask: can you confirm approval process for quotes and final audio?
[08:42] Marta: Yes, give us two business days for transcript and two rounds of edits.
[08:48] Jordan: Perfect. We'll send links and proposed snippets.
[08:52] Alex: We'll also include a 30-second and a 60-second social clip.
[08:56] Marta: Great.
[09:00] Jordan: Thanks everyone, appreciate your time, we'll follow up with assets.
[09:05] [End of recorded segment — translation: remaining minutes are off-the-record chit-chat about logistics and scheduling].

Note: Transcript contains occasional transcription uncertainty (speaker overlaps, proper nouns may be slightly off). The recording is multitrack; producer to splice highlights for a ~20-25 minute public episode and produce short social clips.
